name: PROSTATEx: Prostate Cancer MRI Assessment Challenge
description: The PROSTATEx Challenge dataset is a public multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) benchmark hosted on The Cancer Imaging Archive (TCIA) in collaboration with SPIE, AAPM, and NCI. Curated from examinations performed at Radboud University Medical Center in Nijmegen, Netherlands, the dataset features 346 mpMRI exams from 345 patients acquired on 3T Siemens scanners. Imaging modalities include transverse T2-weighted turbo spin-echo, apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) maps, high b-value diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), and dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) MRI series. Each patient case provides 3D spatial coordinate centroids of confirmed prostate lesions coupled with histopathology-proven clinically significant prostate cancer binary ground truth (Gleason score >= 7).

name: PTB Diagnostic ECG Database
description: The PTB Diagnostic ECG Database is a foundational clinical electrocardiography repository compiled by the National Metrology Institute of Germany (Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt - PTB). It contains 549 high-resolution records from 290 subjects (209 men and 81 women, aged 17 to 87), encompassing healthy volunteers and patients across nine major clinical diagnostic categories: myocardial infarction, cardiomyopathy, heart failure, bundle branch block, dysrhythmia, myocardial hypertrophy, valvular heart disease, and myocarditis. Each record contains 15 simultaneously recorded signals (the 12 standard leads plus 3 orthogonal Frank XYZ leads) sampled at 1,000 Hz with 16-bit resolution. Users should note that this collection is the original 1995 PTB diagnostic database, distinct from the larger 2020 PTB-XL database.

name: PTB-XL+: Comprehensive Electrocardiographic Feature Dataset
description: PTB-XL+ is an extensive clinical feature and annotation dataset complementing the 21,837 twelve-lead ECG records of the canonical PTB-XL database. Developed by the Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt (PTB), Charité Universitätsmedizin Berlin, and Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, it provides fiducial point segmentations (P-onset, P-peak, P-offset, QRS-onset, QRS-peak, J-point, T-offset), morphological wave boundaries, heart rate, electrical axis metrics, and median heartbeat waveforms extracted using validated commercial and academic ECG analysis software (GE Marquette 12SL and Uni-G). The dataset serves as a rich multi-modal bridge between raw 12-lead voltage waveforms, clinical diagnoses, and tabular cardiological features.

name: Raw and Preprocessed EEG of ILS-Screened Verbal–Visual and Active–Reflective Learners during the Short Hagen Matrices Test (HMT-S)
description: This dataset contains 8-channel electroencephalography (EEG) recordings of 28 Indonesian undergraduate students labelled on two Felder–Silverman learning-style dimensions: Verbal–Visual (7 Verbal, 7 Visual) and Active–Reflective (7 Active, 7 Reflective). Participants were screened with an Indonesian translation of the Index of Learning Styles (ILS), and only those with a moderate-to-strong preference (score ≥ 5) on the target dimension were recorded. During recording, participants solved the six items of the short form of the Hagen Matrices Test (HMT-S). Each item was shown for 15 s without and then for 15 s with its answer options (12 stimuli, about 3 min of task EEG). EEG was acquired at 250 Hz with an OpenBCI Cyton board from Fp1, Fp2, F3, F4, C3, C4, O1 and O2 (10–20 system). The data are organized in two tiers: (1) Raw EEG (OpenBCI GUI export, CSV) with the answer log of each participant (XLSX), recording the selected option, the correct option and the time of each answer; (2) Band-pass filtered (8–30 Hz) EEG segmented into non-overlapping 1-s, 250-sample windows aligned to the task phases (CSV; 180 windows × 8 channels per participant). The data can be used for subject-independent classification of learning-style preferences, comparison of filtering, artifact-handling and feature-extraction methods, deep learning on EEG, and analyses relating EEG to task performance. The README file describes every folder, file and column, as well as the known limitations of the data. The files contain no names or other direct personal identifiers.

name: Shongbad Chitro: A Multimodal Bangla News Image-Text Dataset
description: Shongbad Chitro: A Multimodal Bangla News Image-Text Dataset contains 50,000 Bangla news articles and 50,000 associated image files. It supports research in Bangla natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal learning. The recorded publication dates range from 13 August 2023 to 30 August 2026. The articles are organized into nine major categories: বাংলাদেশ (Bangladesh), রাজনীতি (Politics), বিশ্ব (World), বাণিজ্য (Business), মতামত (Opinion), খেলা (Sports), বিনোদন (Entertainment), চাকরি (Jobs), and জীবনযাপন (Lifestyle). The dataset preserves 113 original subcategory labels, providing a two-level structure for broad and detailed news classification. Each article record includes its title, body text, subcategory, major category, publication date, source URL, author, image caption where available, image URL, and local image path. These fields connect textual content with associated images and source information. Major categories were assigned using the source sections recorded in article URLs, supplemented by custom mappings for topics outside the nine-category structure. Education is grouped under Bangladesh, literature under Entertainment, religion and general science and technology under Lifestyle, and freelancing under Jobs. A Category Mapping worksheet documents these groupings and their article counts. The dataset is distributed as an Excel workbook and an images folder. The workbook contains article records, summary statistics, and category mappings. It also retains 86 empty trailing rows, which are excluded from the total of 50,000 articles. Shongbad Chitro can support research on Bangla news classification, hierarchical classification, multimodal topic prediction, image–text retrieval, image captioning, and news summarization.

name: Small and Fast Falling object LiDAR and RGB Dataset
description: This dataset supports the Feature-Fused Three-Frame (FF3F) framework for detecting and tracking small, fast-moving objects using LiDAR. It contains 480 Intel RealSense L515 recordings, divided into training, validation and test sets of 160 recordings each. Each set includes 40 recordings of vertical free fall, rolling-to-edge fall, bounce/rebound and cluttered-background free fall. The release includes depth recordings, timestamps, camera parameters, background measurements, manually annotated bounding boxes and visibility states, source code, trained models, calibration mappings and evaluation results. It supports reproduction of tracking, motion-estimation, component-ablation and confidence-calibration results, together with validation-recording alert replay. Three-dimensional reference positions are derived from the annotations and the same LiDAR measurements, rather than independent motion measurements. Alert timing represents timestamp-paced replay, not live warning delivery. RGB recordings were recorded but not used in these experiments and are excluded from this release.

name: A dataset for soybean yield prediction (Machine Learning applications)
description: The dataset combines meteorological, soil and soybean yield data collected from three publicly available sources: the Brazilian National Institute of Meteorology (Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia - INMET), the Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics (Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística - IBGE), and the International Soil Reference and Information Centre (ISRIC). The final dataset consists of 765 observations and 37 variables. Each observation corresponds to a municipality-harvest instance and is associated with the soybean yield observed at the end of the growing season. Meteorological variables were derived from hourly measurements collected by INMET and aggregated using simple averages over the period from October 10 to December 31, lacking two-months for the harvest in February (the growing cycle of soybean was assumed as approximately 125 days). This two-month forecasting horizon has been adopted in previous crop yield prediction studies using Machine Learning applications. Soil variables were collected at the municipality level and used as static features, while additional engineered variables were extracted from the raw meteorological data.

name: A Sri Lankan dataset of Tibial shaft X-ray images for fracture detection and classification
description: This dataset includes tibial shaft X-rays collected from Ashraf Memorial Hospital, Kalmunai. This dataset can be used for tasks like object detection, image analysis, fracture classification, and segmentation. The X-ray images were organized into 2 folders, which are annotated data and raw data. The X-ray images are further organized into annotated and raw data. The annotated dataset contains 253 fractured tibial shaft X-ray images, with fracture regions annotated for object detection. The raw data include 244 non-fractured tibial shaft X-ray images collected from 204 patients, together with the corresponding raw images of the annotated fractured cases. All the images are in .jpg, .png or .jpeg format. The annotated images and associated annotations can be used for fracture-region localization and object detection, while the classified fractured and non-fractured images can be used for binary fracture classification and related medical image analysis tasks. The fractured data is split into training and testing sets in a 70:30 ratio. Dataset collection: • Source: Ashraf Memorial Hospital, Kalmunai • Capture Method: Collected from PACS (Picture Archiving and Communication System) and using a phone camera. • Anonymization: All data were rigorously anonymized to maintain confidentiality and privacy. Dataset composition: • Total Participants: 438 patients, totalling 497 images. Anterior-Posterior (AP) and Lateral (L) views were obtained from both male and female patients aged between 18 and 65 years. Variables: • Fragmentary segmental fracture: 17 • Fragmented wedge fracture: 22 • Intact segmental fracture:7 • Intact wedge fracture: 74 • Oblique fracture: 38 • Spiral fracture: 30 • Transverse fracture: 65 • Non-fracture: 244

name: St Petersburg INCART 12-lead Arrhythmia Database
description: The St Petersburg INCART 12-lead Arrhythmia Database is a public clinical electrocardiogram database contributed to PhysioNet by the St. Petersburg Institute of Cardiological Technics (INCART) in St. Petersburg, Russia. The database consists of 75 annotated 30-minute 12-lead ECG recordings extracted from 32 Holter records of patients undergoing evaluation for coronary artery disease. Sampled at 257 Hz per lead, recordings capture diverse cardiac morphologies and rhythm disturbances, including premature ventricular complexes, bundle branch blocks, supraventricular arrhythmias, and ischemic transient ST-segment shifts. Each record contains over 175,000 reference beat annotations verified by expert cardiologists, making it an essential reference dataset for multi-lead automated arrhythmia detection.

name: STAFF III Database: Acutely Induced Myocardial Ischemia ECGs
description: The STAFF III Database is an experimental clinical study recorded at the Charleston Area Medical Center in West Virginia by Lund University, Duke University, and University of Zaragoza. It comprises continuous high-resolution standard 12-lead ECGs recorded from 104 patients undergoing elective percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PTCA). Balloon inflations produced controlled, acutely induced regional myocardial ischemia lasting up to several minutes. The collection captures pre-inflation, peak inflation, and post-deflation reperfusion ECG states, offering in vivo human data for studying the spatio-temporal evolution of acute ischemic cardiac injury.

description: The Sugar Beets 2016 dataset is a multi-sensor agricultural robotics dataset recorded by the Institute of Geodesy and Geoinformation (IPB) at the University of Bonn and the German Research Foundation (DFG). name: A Synchronized Chittagonian Speech Corpus for Dialect ASR and Speech Translation
description: This dataset presents a synchronized Chittagonian speech corpus developed for low-resource speech processing and dialect translation. The corpus contains 8,004 Chittagonian speech samples paired with corresponding Chittagonian transcripts and Standard Bangla translations. The textual component of the dataset is taken from the publicly available Kothon dataset, a Chittagonian–Standard Bangla parallel text resource. In this work, the original text pairs were extended with newly collected speech recordings from native Chittagonian speakers, creating a synchronized speech-text corpus for automatic speech recognition (ASR), speech-to-speech translation, machine translation, dialect normalization, and text-to-speech (TTS) . The dataset is organized into predefined training, validation, and test splits containing 6,403, 801, and 800 samples, respectively. Each audio recording is provided in WAV format. This resource aims to support reproducible research on Chittagonian, an under-resourced regional variety of Bangla, by enabling the development and evaluation of machine learning models for dialect-aware speech and language technologies.

description: TotalSegmentator is a foundational open-source computed tomography (CT) segmentation dataset and toolkit developed by researchers at the Department of Radiology, University Hospital Basel. name: UIA-IOT-IDS dataset: Comprehensive IoT network intrusion detection and sensor-anomaly
description: This record contains two complementary, fully labelled datasets for machine-learning-based IoT security, together with the complete acquisition and analysis code. All data were collected from a single physical smart-home testbed at the University of Agder (Grimstad, Norway), built around a resource-constrained Raspberry Pi 3 gateway, five ESP8266 + DHT22 temperature/humidity nodes in distinct rooms, a PySense board, a Flask IoT server with InfluxDB storage, and three Kali Linux attacker VMs. Network flows were computed on-device in real time by a custom tcpdump-based extractor, so no raw PCAP is stored. The deposit is organised into two datasets that serve two tasks: (1) IDS_Dataset - network-flow INTRUSION DETECTION. The "Original" folder holds the raw, as-collected flows: 3,637,408 labelled bidirectional records across 54 classes, each described by 75 columns (6 identifier/metadata fields + 69 statistical features) plus a label. Of the 69 features, 46 are schema-compatible with CIC-IoT-2023 and 23 are additional bidirectional descriptors (per-direction packet counts, packet-length and inter-arrival-time statistics, and flow rates). The "Balanced" folder holds a cleaned, SMOTE-balanced version: 1,415,074 records, one CSV per class, with identifier and zero-variance columns removed (64 features + label). The taxonomy spans 51 attack sub-types in nine categories - Reconnaissance, DoS, DDoS, Brute Force, Web-based, Mirai, Spoofing, False Data Injection and Backdoor/C2 - plus three benign traffic types (sensor, SSH, Grafana). It reproduces the eight CIC-IoT-2023 categories and adds families absent from common benchmarks: False Data Injection (direct injection and man-in-the-middle sensor replay) and Backdoor/command-and-control beaconing. (2) AD_Dataset - sensor ANOMALY DETECTION. The "Benign" folder holds timestamped temperature and humidity readings from the five DHT22 nodes (one CSV per node); the "Abnormal" folder holds readings from three anomaly sources: a heat-biased PySense board (hardware fault), direct false-data injection, and ARP-spoofing replay. 4,253,024 readings fall within the 1 March - 13 April 2026 window analysed in the article; earlier readings are also included. Each reading is stored as one row carrying either a temperature or a humidity value (InfluxDB export format). All tabular data are UTF-8 CSV files with a header row; every network-flow record carries an explicit label. The deposit also includes the full code: the real-time flow extractor, the Flask server with intentionally vulnerable endpoints, the attack and injection scripts, the SMOTE preprocessing, and the model code (XGBoost benchmark, LSTM-autoencoder, MAML, Prototypical Networks). A disjoint base/novel class split supports supervised, unsupervised and few-shot detection research.

name: UzSER-MFCC
description: This dataset provides acoustic features for speech emotion recognition (SER) in Uzbek, a low-resource Turkic language. It is derived from 598 emotional speech utterances (26.5 min in total; 0.41–4.99 s, mean 2.66 s) segmented from the dialogue of three Uzbek-language feature films (Novda, Tinchlik ortida, Vasiyat) publicly available on YouTube. The utterances were spoken by approximately 12–13 speakers (about 4 female and 8–9 male) and were labelled by four annotators into six emotion classes: anger (ANG, 101), disgust (DIS, 108), fear (FEA, 106), happiness (HAP, 73), neutral (NEU, 106) and sadness (SAD, 104). Source audio was decoded with FFmpeg and standardised to 16 kHz, 16-bit, mono PCM before feature extraction. Because the source films are protected by copyright, raw audio is not distributed. Instead, the dataset contains: (1) metadata.csv – one row per utterance with emotion label, source film, duration and signal-quality measures; (2) features/utterance_mfcc40_stats.csv – 400 utterance-level statistics computed from 40 MFCCs and their first- and second-order derivatives; (3) features/frame_mfcc13/ – frame-level 13-dimensional MFCC matrices (NumPy .npy, 25 ms Hamming window, 10 ms hop) for every utterance; (4) tables/ and figures/ – descriptive statistics, class distributions and baseline results; (5) scripts/ – the complete Python code for feature extraction, statistics, figures and baseline classification. Baseline stratified 5-fold cross-validation on the utterance-level features gives 45.8% accuracy (UAR 0.449) for an SVM and 47.0% accuracy (UAR 0.462) for a random forest, against a chance level of 16.7%. The emotions are unevenly distributed across the three films, so film-aware evaluation is recommended (see README.md). The dataset can be used for benchmarking SER methods, cross-lingual and transfer-learning experiments, and feature-level research for Uzbek.

name: VegHealth14: A Multi-Crop Leaf Disease Image Dataset of 14 Commonly Cultivated Vegetables in Bangladesh
description: VegHealth14 is a leaf image dataset for classifying the health condition of 14 vegetables that are widely grown in Bangladesh: bean, bitter gourd, bottle gourd, cabbage, cauliflower, chilli, cucumber, eggplant, okra, potato, radish, ridge gourd, snake gourd and tomato. It contains 53 classes. Each crop has one healthy class and between two and six classes of disease or pest damage. The conditions include fungal diseases (downy mildew, anthracnose, Alternaria spot, leaf mold, late blight), bacterial diseases (bacterial spot, bacterial wilt, black rot), viral diseases (mosaic virus, leaf curl virus, yellow leaf curl virus) and damage from jassids, leaf-eating insects, insect egg masses and mites. The images were gathered from several publicly available open-source datasets and combined into a single collection with a consistent class structure. The source images came in many sizes, from 128×128 to 6000×4000 pixels, and in JPEG, PNG, and WebP formats. Preprocessing 1. Files in each class folder were renamed to sequential numbers (1.jpg, 2.jpg, 3.jpg and so on). 2. Every image was resized to two standard resolutions, 224×224 and 512×512 pixels. Images were scaled directly to a square without cropping or padding, so the whole leaf stays in the frame, but non-square photos are slightly stretched. 3. All images were converted to RGB JPEG (8-bit, quality 95). PNG and WebP files were converted to JPEG. 4. Exact duplicate images were identified by MD5 hash. Some source datasets already contained oversampled copies, so the combined collection includes 11,421 files that duplicate another image in the same class and 157 images that appear in two classes. Some source images were smaller than the target size and had to be enlarged: Cabbage (150×150), Snake Gourd (128×128 to 224×224), Potato and some Tomato and Cauliflower images (256×256). These look softer than the rest, especially at 512×512. Augmentation The augmented versions balance the dataset to exactly 1,000 images per class. Only unique images were used as the base for augmentation: exact duplicates within a class were removed first, and images found in more than one class were excluded. Two classes had more than 1,000 unique images (Eggplant Healthy and Eggplant Mosaic Virus Disease), so 1,000 were randomly selected (seed 42). The two Potato blight classes already had exactly 1,000 and were not augmented. For every other class, augmented images were added until the class reached 1,000. The following techniques were used, alone or in combination: Rotation: 90°, 180° or 270° clockwise Flipping: horizontal or vertical Centre zoom crop: the central 90% or 80% of the image, resized back to full size Corner zoom crop: the top-left, top-right, bottom-left or bottom-right 85% of the image, resized back to full size Total image before augmentation: 27,282 Total image after augmentation: 53000

name: A Visual and Thermal Imaging Dataset of Lemon Fruits Following Controlled Hot-Water Treatment
description: This dataset contains visual and thermal image data collected from 140 lemon fruits (Citrus limon) to investigate surface appearance and thermal responses following controlled hot-water treatment. which was maintained consistently across all image files and processing outputs. The specific cultivar of the lemons was not independently verified. It has been developed and annotated in College of Engineering, Nanjing Agricultural University, Nanjing 210031, China, For each lemon, two visual images were acquired from operationally designated V and H views using the main rear camera of an iPhone 16 Pro Max (48 MP; f/1.78). The smartphone was mounted on a tripod at a fixed distance of 18 cm from the fruit. The lemon was placed on printed blue-grid graph paper, with major grid lines spaced 1.0 cm apart to provide a spatial reference. The fruit was repositioned between acquisitions to obtain the second view. the views are designated operationally as V and H rather than being assumed to be perfectly orthogonal. Thermal images were acquired before and after a controlled hot-water treatment. An initial thermal image (T₀) was recorded before treatment. Each lemon was then fully submerged individually in boiling water maintained at approximately °C for 60 s using a mesh holder. After removal from the water, the fruit was blotted dry using a consistent procedure. Thermal images were acquired using a UNI-T UTi165A handheld infrared thermal imager (160 × 120 pixels; NETD: 50 mK; stated accuracy: ±2 °C or ±2%). The thermal camera was mounted at a fixed distance of 15 cm, with emissivity set to 0.95 and the rainbow colour palette selected. Five additional thermal images were recorded immediately after treatment (T₁) and at 1, 2, 3, and 4 min after treatment (T₂–T₅). The dataset consists exclusively of image data and includes multiple representations of the acquired visual and thermal images. These include: - Raw visual images from the V and H views. - Segmented visual images containing the isolated lemon regions. - Corresponding visual image masks. - Raw thermal images acquired at six time points (T₀–T₅). - Thermal images preserved in TIFF format. - Segmented thermal images containing the isolated lemon regions. - Corresponding thermal image masks. In total, 1,120 primary images were acquired from the 140 lemons, comprising 280 visual images (two views per lemon) and 840 thermal images (six time points per lemon). Additional segmented images, masks, and TIFF-format files are provided as processed or preserved versions of the corresponding primary image data. where applicable, view and thermal time-point labels. Sample inclusion or exclusion was based solely on image quality and was independent of any external target or measurement values. The dataset is intended to provide traceable raw and processed visual and thermal image data for lemon imaging, segmentation, thermal-response analysis, and related computer vision or machine learning research.

name: WeedVision-14: A Field-Scale Image Dataset for Multi-Species Weed Detection and Segmentation Task
description: WeedVision-14 is a multi-format labeled image dataset comprising 10,461 RGB images of 14 weed species commonly found in major cereal cropping systems of the Indo-Gangetic Plain, India. The images were collected at the experimental research field of ICAR-Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI), New Delhi (28°38′N, 77°09′E), under natural field conditions during the cropping season, with variations in illumination, background, viewing angle, camera distance, and weed growth conditions. After field collection, the images were pre-processed and standardized to a uniform resolution of 512 × 512 pixels. The dataset covers major weed types, including narrow-leaf (grass) weeds (Bermuda Grass and Crowfoot Grass), sedge weed (Rice Sedge), and broadleaf weeds (Green Amaranth, Lamb's Quarters, Nettle-leaved Goosefoot, Benghal Dayflower, Field Bindweed, Lesser Swine Cress, Common Mallow, Burclover, Congress Grass, Stonebreaker, and Horse Purslane). The dataset supports core computer vision tasks, including weed classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation. The dataset was labeled under expert supervision, with bounding-box annotations and pixel-level segmentation masks generated to support weed detection and segmentation, respectively. The bounding-box annotations define the spatial extent of individual weed plants and are provided in YOLO, Pascal VOC, and COCO formats, while the segmentation masks represent the corresponding weed regions at the pixel level and are provided as binary and multiclass masks. The dataset contains 16,079 detection instances and 20,414 segmentation mask instances across all 14 weed classes. WeedVision-14 provides a standardized resource for developing and evaluating computer vision models for automated weed identification, detection, and segmentation.

name: YemSarc: A Multimodal Benchmark Dataset for Sarcasm Detection in Yemeni and Related Arabic Dialects
description: YemSarc is the first multimodal (text, audio, and video) benchmark dataset for sarcasm detection in Yemeni dialectal Arabic and seven additional Arabic dialects. It comprises 630 balanced utterances (315 sarcastic, 315 non-sarcastic) drawn from naturally occurring conversational exchanges across eight Arabic dialects: Mahwiti, Ibbi, Adeni, Sanaani, Dhamari, Saudi, Egyptian, and Taizzi. Each target utterance is paired with its preceding conversational context and is represented across three synchronized modalities: written transcript, audio segment, and video frame sequence. The dataset was constructed from two widely popular Yemeni comedic drama series (Bayt Al-Madaliz and Khuruj Nihai), sourced from their official YouTube channels. Annotation was carried out through a structured three-phase protocol by three expert academic linguists, achieving a final inter-annotator agreement of Fleiss' Kappa = 0.7473. The dataset is released with a fully reproducible, speaker-independent, and statistically audited evaluation pipeline. This dataset is intended for non-commercial academic research purposes, including multimodal sarcasm detection, Arabic dialectal NLP, and social media analysis. The dataset is licensed under CC BY 4.0.
